name: Air Purifiers
hub_intro: Irish homes have an indoor air problem nobody talks about: damp-driven mould spores, dust mites thriving in humidity, pollen seasons that now run March to September, and solid-fuel smoke drifting through winter estates. A true HEPA purifier removes 99.95%+ of these particles. We compare real performance — CADR, filter costs, noise — across every budget.
guide: HEPA means H13 or it doesn't mean much

Look for 'True HEPA' H13/H14 — filters capturing 99.95%+ of 0.3-micron particles. 'HEPA-type' or 'HEPA-like' is marketing for lesser filters. For Irish mould spores (1–20 microns) and pollen (10–100 microns), genuine H13 catches essentially everything.

Clean Air Delivery Rate tells you how much purified air the unit moves. Match it to your room: you want the room's volume cleaned 3–5 times per hour. A typical 20 m² Irish living room (~50 m³) needs a CADR of 150–250 m³/h minimum.
Filter costs are the real price

A €150 purifier with €60 annual filters costs more over five years than a €250 unit with €30 filters. We factor replacement costs into every recommendation — it's where cheap brands claw their money back.

Run continuously on low/auto rather than blasting occasionally — particle levels rebound within hours. Place 30+ cm from walls, ideally in the room you sleep in: you spend a third of your life there breathing its air.

faqs.q: Do air purifiers help with mould in Irish homes?
faqs.a: They capture airborne mould spores (H13 HEPA catches them efficiently) which reduces spread and inhalation — but they don't fix the moisture source. The winning combo for damp Irish homes is dehumidifier (stops growth) + purifier (clears spores).

faqs.q: Do air purifiers help with hay fever?
faqs.a: Significantly, for indoor relief. Running a HEPA purifier in the bedroom with windows closed during pollen season measurably cuts indoor pollen. Sufferers report better sleep within days. Pair with showering before bed during peak grass pollen (May–July in Ireland).

faqs.q: What size air purifier do I need?
faqs.a: Match CADR to room volume: aim for 3–5 air changes per hour. Bedroom (~30 m³): CADR 100–150. Living room (~50 m³): CADR 150–250. Open-plan (~80 m³+): CADR 300+. Undersized purifiers running flat-out are loud and ineffective.

faqs.q: How much do air purifiers cost to run in Ireland?
faqs.a: Very little: most run 5–30 W on low/auto — roughly €1–3 per month running continuously. The real cost is filters: €25–70 per year depending on brand. Check filter prices before buying the machine.

faqs.q: Air purifier or dehumidifier for an Irish home?
faqs.a: Different jobs: dehumidifiers remove moisture (fixing mould's cause, condensation, damp), purifiers remove particles (spores, pollen, dust, smoke). Damp/mould house: dehumidifier first. Allergies/asthma: purifier first. Many Irish homes genuinely benefit from both.

faqs.q: Are air purifiers worth it for asthma?
faqs.a: Clinical evidence supports HEPA filtration reducing airborne triggers — dust mite allergen, pollen, mould spores, smoke. Many Irish asthma sufferers report fewer night symptoms with a bedroom purifier. They complement, never replace, prescribed treatment. This is general information, not medical advice.

faqs.q: Do air purifiers remove smells and smoke?
faqs.a: Only models with substantial activated carbon filters handle odours and gases — thin carbon sheets do little. For turf/wood smoke drifting in, or cooking smells, prioritise units with 0.5 kg+ carbon. HEPA alone removes smoke particles but not the smell.

faqs.q: Should I sleep with an air purifier on?
faqs.a: Yes — night mode exists for exactly this. Bedroom air quality matters most during your 8 sleeping hours. Pick a unit that drops below 25 dB in sleep mode with display-off, and let it run all night on auto.
